title: Runbook Stitcher: telemetry-driven micro-runbook composition for rapid remediation
creator: Avery Chen
description:
Problem: Oncall escalations frequently require stitching together multiple small remediation steps (prefix cache clears, model failover, quota bump, traffic routing). Engineers waste time manually mapping telemetry signals to the correct sequence of safe actions.

Solution: Build a lightweight "Runbook Stitcher" service that listens to prioritized telemetry signals and proposes a ranked set of runlet sequences (micro-runbooks) that can be executed as idempotent tasks in the admin console or via CLI. The Stitcher composes pre-verified tasklets from the operator library, annotates required context (request id, model/version, shard), and annotates safety gates (RBAC, dry-run, approval step).

Core components:
- Signal adapter: normalized event shapes from metrics, tracing, and SLO alerts.
- Composer: rule engine + small ML ranking model that maps signals and recent incident context to candidate sequences.
- Verification layer: static checks (idempotency, permission level), automated dry-run simulator, and test prompt execution in canary tenancy.
- Execution surface: runlet orchestration API integrated with existing admin-task-runner (supports canary rollout and rollback).
- Observability: per-runlet provenance (which signals triggered it), execution timeline, and cost/latency delta metrics.

Goals: reduce mean time to recovery (MTTR) for common remediation classes by 30% within two sprints, and enable first-line support to safely execute remediations without escalation.

Tradeoffs considered:
- Strength of automation vs safety: we prefer suggested runlets that require one-click approval for high-risk actions. Low-risk actions can be auto-triggered behind a feature flag.
- Rule-based vs model-driven composition: start with deterministic rules + heuristics, ship quickly, gather signal-to-action telemetry, and iterate with a small ranking model if helpful.

Integration notes: the Stitcher will use existing operator task spec format (see ENG-314271) and will publish provenance events to the admin-telemetry topic. It requires KMS access for any credentialed steps and RBAC checks against the console permission API.

Deliverables: design doc, prototype composer, 10 prebuilt runlets for the top 3 incident classes, CLI +/- console integration, rollout plan with feature flag and kill-switch, and acceptance telemetry dashboard.
acceptance_criteria: Stitcher proposes a relevant 1-5 step micro-runbook for 85% of test incidents from our evaluation corpus
Admin console shows provenance for each proposed runlet and a visible approval gate for high-risk steps
Dry-run simulator executes steps in a sandbox and reports expected outcome without side effects
End-to-end test: on a synthetic alert, a support engineer can execute recommended runlets and return the system to healthy state within 25 minutes
Telemetry: MTTR for the targeted incident classes decreases by >=20% in rollout pilot
